text:
maya: :warning: customer reported admin actions observed from a service principal originating from an IP outside the customer's VPC allowlist. attaching snippets from control-plane audit and KMS logs.

maya: logs:```2026-03-20T18:03:12Z KMS decrypt key=projects/prod/keys/ctrlplane-key principal=svcacct:edge-proxy@tenanta src_ip=3.121.45.22 action=Decrypt status=OK``````2026-03-20T18:03:13Z audit:control-plane user=svcacct:edge-proxy@tenanta verb=kubectl exec namespace=redwood-admin command=kubectl exec -it pod/ctl -- /bin/sh src_ip=3.121.45.22``````rbac PR merged last night: github.com/redwood/rbac/compare/refactor-subject-matcher #1123```

maya: customer says their VPC allowlist doesn't include 3.121.45.22. looks like a principal matched despite being outside allowed CIDRs.

tom: :eyes: is that IP a NAT egress from our dedicated region or definitely external? can you paste the full audit record?

maya: full audit attached above. checked our egress list — not in customer's allowlist. note: the refactor changed subject matcher to prefix-matching for service principals (fast path) instead of exact equality. hypothesis: "svcacct:edge-proxy@tenanta" is being matched by a rule intended for "svcacct:edge@tenanta" due to startsWith logic.

jess: if subject matcher is startsWith that's a serious regression for dedicated/private allowlists. we should treat principal ids as opaque exact strings. preparing rollback PR now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by jess for rbac PR #1123 — rollback stage 1/3 (rbac-service), 2/3 queued.

security: audit-bot shows 3 KMS decrypt events by that principal in the last 30m. recommend immediate token revocation and consider key rotation. also gather all control-plane admin verbs executed by that principal.

maya: mitigation plan (taking actions now):
1) revoke service account tokens for edge-proxy in tenant-a:```kubectl -n tenanta delete secret $(kubectl -n tenanta get sa edge-proxy -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}')```
2) add temporary deny rule on control-plane-proxy for source IP 3.121.45.22 and similar ranges.
3) run search for other principals that could be shadowed by prefix match:```SELECT principal FROM rbac_bindings WHERE subject LIKE 'svcacct:%' AND LENGTH(subject) < 40; -- quick heuristic```

tom: i'll run a repo-wide grep for startsWith/substring matching in RBAC code (rbac/* matcher utils).

jess: hotfix PR ready — enforce exact match on principalID and add the tenant+uuid tag to principal creation so future refactors can use stable id matching. adding unit + integration test to CI to detect shadowing. PR: github.com/redwood/rbac/pull/1125

deploy-bot: Hotfix deployed to staging (rbac-service). Smoke tests passed. Rolling to prod in 10m.

security: also recommend rotating the KMS key used for control-plane secrets (ctrlplane-key) and revoking any issued session tokens tied to that principal. I'll open a key rotation runbook.

audit-bot: quick query results: found 2 additional principals in last 24h that would have matched the old prefix logic (list attached).

maya: opened customer incident update. telling them we have mitigations and a rollback in flight; recommending rotation of any app-level credentials touched by control-plane actions.

jess: postmortem owner = jess. action items: (A) revert subject prefix matcher to exact match, (B) add CI detection for principal-shadowing, (C) increase KMS audit retention to 30d for dedicated/private, (D) add policy to require uuid tag on service principals.

security: :lock: classifying this as P2 (customer-impact, limited scope) — will escalate if we see more decrypts or additional external IPs.

tom: scanning merges now, will post hits to this thread.

maya: after rollback and token revocation, control-plane access from 3.121.45.22 stopped. monitoring for 1h.

audit-bot: scheduled follow-up: run full RBAC subject-sanity scan across all dedicated/private tenants in 2h and report anomalies.

maya: thanks all — keep thread updated. ping me if deploy shows more oddities. :white_check_mark:
